paper.title: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine
paper.shortTitle: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine
paper.authors: PolackFernando P., ThomasStephen J., KitchinNicholas et al.

thesis: A two-dose regimen of BNT162b2 conferred 95% protection against Covid-19 in persons 16 years of age or older.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What effect or association is supported in the studied human population?

nodes.title: Choose cohort and endpoint
nodes.body: In an ongoing multinational, placebo-controlled, observer-blinded, pivotal efficacy trial, we randomly assigned persons 16 years of age or older in a 1:1 ratio to receive two doses, 21 days apart, of either placebo or the BNT162b2 vaccine candidate (30 μg per dose).

nodes.title: Measure human outcomes
nodes.body: A total of 43,548 participants underwent randomization, of whom 43,448 received injections: 21,720 with BNT162b2 and 21,728 with placebo.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: There were 8 cases of Covid-19 with onset at least 7 days after the second dose among participants assigned to receive BNT162b2 and 162 cases among those assigned to placebo; BNT162b2 was 95% effective in preventing Covid-19 (95% credible interval, 90.3 to 97.6).

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: A two-dose regimen of BNT162b2 conferred 95% protection against Covid-19 in persons 16 years of age or older.
